findings.text: Minimum per run queue runtime reserve equals one millisecond.
Minimum bandwidth expiration guard interval equals two milliseconds and is used to suppress slack distribution near a refresh boundary.
Bandwidth slack period equals five milliseconds.

Period handler deactivates when no bandwidth limit applies. Otherwise it counts elapsed periods, refills burst allowance even when marked idle, stays active only if throttled work exists, marks future idleness when unthrottled, accounts throttled periods, repeatedly releases bandwidth while surplus remains, then clears idle and stays active. Its Boolean style result signals deactivate versus continue.

Slack handler clears its started flag, exits when a periodic refresh is imminent, exits when unlimited or when pooled runtime does not exceed one slice, otherwise distributes pooled surplus outside the bandwidth lock.

Period timer advances through every expired period and invokes the period handler per overrun. After more than three invocations in one expiry it doubles period, quota and burst unless that would exceed the maximum quota period, emitting a rate limited warning in either case, then resets its counter. It deactivates and stops when the handler reports idle, otherwise it restarts.

Slack timer entry resolves its container bandwidth object, runs the slack handler, and never restarts. Period timer entry resolves its container, processes all overruns under a bandwidth guard, records active state, and restarts unless idle.

Period handler requires the bandwidth lock on entry, drops it with interrupts restored while distributing runtime because distribution cannot nest that lock, then reacquires it. Slack and update paths use scoped or class guards on the same lock. Run queue iteration paths assert run queue ownership, hold RCU across the task group list, and bracket offline unthrottling with run queue clock loop updates.
No-hz idle balancing state holds an idle CPU mask, a blocked load flag, a needs update flag, plus next balance and next blocked times measured in jiffies, placed cache line aligned.

Runtime enablement mirrors whether the group quota is limited for the local CPU queue. Offline handling skips active CPUs, disables future throttling on bandwidth controlled queues, and for already throttled queues installs a minimal remaining quantum before unthrottling without advancing task time. Stop tick handling preserves the tick dependency only when bandwidth is in use, the CPU is full no-hz, exactly one entity runs, and the selected task is bandwidth constrained.
Alternate builds provide empty inline forms for runtime enablement, offline unthrottling and stop tick update, meaning those operations are compiled out.

A run queue is eligible for scheduler idle selection when it is in scheduler idle state and the candidate does not itself use the idle policy. A CPU is an eligible idle target when it is available idle or its queue satisfies that scheduler idle test.
Delayed count is the difference between queued and runnable hierarchical fair counts on the run queue.
Three per CPU CPU masks are reserved for load balancing, wakeup destination selection, and balance decision scratch use.

Load, runnable and utilization queries without a task return the full CPU metric when the task is on another CPU or has no averaging history; otherwise they subtract the task hierarchical load, runnable average, or utilization contribution with saturation. Reads of shared averages are single atomic style loads.

Wakee accounting decays the current flip count by half at most once per second tick interval, then records a new flip only when the woken task differs from the previous wakee. Wide wakeup compares the larger and smaller flip counts against the last level cache size factor and reports wide only when both exceed the factor scaled threshold.

Idle wake affinity prefers the previous CPU when both this and previous are idle and share cache, else this CPU when it is idle and cache shared; under synchronous wakeup it prefers this CPU when only one non delayed entity runs there; then it prefers an idle previous CPU, else reports no candidate. Weight based affinity compares capacity scaled effective loads including the task, optionally biased and adjusted by domain imbalance, with a synchronous tie adjustment toward stacking. The dispatcher tries idle then weight forms according to feature toggles, counts attempts, and only moves when the result selects the waker CPU.

Destination CPU choice inside a group returns the sole member for single member groups. Otherwise over allowed CPUs with matching core cookie it immediately takes a scheduler idle queue, else remembers the idle CPU with smallest exit latency and, on ties or absence, the most recently idled one, else tracks the least loaded busy CPU. An idle candidate wins over any busy candidate.
Idle state lookup either asserts some RCU read hold and returns the run queue cached idle state, or unconditionally returns absence, depending on build.

Wakeup destination search first requires overlap between domain span and task affinity and synchronizes task averages except on fork. It descends only domains carrying the requested flag, asks for a destination group, converts it to a CPU, then continues at the narrower domain level belonging to either the old or new CPU based on span weights until no narrower flagged domain remains.

Wakeup group selection skips groups without allowed CPUs or cookie match, records the local group, gathers per group wakeup statistics, and tracks the best remote group. It refuses migration when no remote exists, when local affinity excludes local, when local is strictly less loaded by type, and applies type specific rules for overloaded, misfit, spare and NUMA locality including imbalance tolerance, preferred node and idle CPU count comparisons.

Group wakeup statistics start cleared, assume misfit under asymmetric capacity until a fitting CPU is found, sum load, utilization and runnable without the task, count runnable and total running excluding a currently running instance of the task, count idle CPUs only when adjusted running count is zero and the CPU passes the without task idle test, then attach capacity and weight, classify the group, and compute scaled average load only for fully busy or overloaded groups.
A CPU is considered idle without a task only when its current entity is either its idle thread or that task and it has no pending wakeups; the caller must have already adjusted the running count.

Period expiry mutates period, quota and burst scaling state while holding only the bandwidth guard and may warn; concurrent readers of those tunables must tolerate growth. Distribution runs without the bandwidth lock so throttled state must be rechecked after reacquiring. Offline unthrottle forcibly installs runnable state with a synthetic quantum on a non advancing clock.
